issue.title: EKS IRSA Elasticsearch amazon_s3_exception 403 access denied in snapshot repositories
issue.body:
## Bug Report
**What did you do?**
Configured Elasticsearch S3 snapshot repository according to the documentation of using EKS IRSA method 
 https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/cloud-on-k8s/master/k8s-snapshots.html#k8s-iam-service-accounts.

This error started with the default `2Gi` pod memory requests and limits, but after checking https://github.com/elastic/cloud-on-k8s/issues/6414, I found that increasing the memory would solve the problem.
First I increased the memory to `4Gi` and the error continued, then `8Gi`, and finally `10Gi`, and to my surprise the error still persisted.

Currently Elasticsearch JVM Heap Size:
```
kubectl exec -it elastic-es-master-0 -n logging -- curl -u "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD" --insecure "https://elastic-es-http.logging.svc.cluster.local:9200/_cat/nodes?h=heap*&v"
Defaulted container "elasticsearch" out of: elasticsearch, elastic-internal-init-filesystem (init), elastic-internal-suspend (init), sysctl (init)
heap.current heap.percent heap.max
       3.3gb           56      6gb
       1.2gb           20      6gb
       3.2gb           65      5gb
       2.1gb           42      5gb
         2gb           33      6gb
       2.4gb           49      5gb
```

**What did you expect to see?**
Successful connection to the S3 repository without any future disruptions.

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**
The initial connection to S3 repository works fine on the first days, but sometimes it gives the snapshot repository error.
Restarting the Elasticsearch Statefulset for both master and data nodes solves the problem, and it **needs to be done every time the error reappears**.

**Environment**

* ECK version:

	2.6.1

* Kubernetes information:

	* EKS 1.27

* Master and Data nodes resources definition:
```
spec:
  nodeSets:
  - name: master
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: elasticsearch
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: 10Gi
            limits:
              memory: 10Gi
          env:
          - name: AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE
            value: "/usr/share/elasticsearch/config/repository-s3/aws-web-identity-token-file" 
          - name: AWS_ROLE_ARN
            value: arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/s3-backups-role
          volumeMounts:
          - name: aws-iam-token
            mountPath: /usr/share/elasticsearch/config/repository-s3
        volumes:
          - name: aws-iam-token
            projected:
              sources:
              - serviceAccountToken:
                  audience: sts.amazonaws.com
                  expirationSeconds: 86400
                  path: aws-web-identity-token-file
```

body:
ES indeed doesn't watch for changes in the token file, but nevertheless the changes in the web Identity token file should be automatically picked up when a role session expires (the default duration is an hour). When the session expires, `STSAssumeRoleWithWebIdentitySessionCredentialsProvider` should [re-read](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-java/blob/abae667a5c4027c685a26b0d717af137e64c100d/aws-java-sdk-sts/src/main/java/com/amazonaws/auth/STSAssumeRoleWithWebIdentitySessionCredentialsProvider.java#L146) the file and use the new token for establishing a new session.

I wonder if there's some duration mismatch, so when the old token expires, but the AWS SDK still consider the session from valid and only invalidates it after a restart.

In the meantime, I also looked at `S3Service` and we don't refresh the credentials when the S3 repository is reloaded with new settings. We should do that so at least users don't need to restart the pod.

I will look further at the issue, because I assumed that the token update workflow should work transparently with the AWS SDK.
Any news on this? @arteam This is a major problem IMHO
